title: Building a Long-Term Working Relationship with a Freelancer
h1: Building a long-term working relationship with a freelancer
description: How to turn a good first project into a lasting freelance relationship: trial work, documentation, regular communication, fair pay, retainers and feedback.
intro: Finding a freelancer who understands your business, communicates well and delivers quality work takes effort. Once you find one, keeping them saves time and money on every future project: no repeated briefing, fewer revisions and a growing understanding of your brand. Long-term relationships do not happen by accident, though. They are built on clear expectations, fair treatment and good communication. This article explains how to turn a successful first project into a lasting working relationship.

faq.a: An agreement to pay for a set amount of work or availability each month, often at a predictable rate.

faq.q: Should I offer long-term work after one project?
faq.a: Consider a few projects first to see consistency, then discuss a longer arrangement.

faq.q: How do I give feedback without damaging the relationship?
faq.a: Be specific, focus on the work, mention what went well and explain why changes are needed.

faq.q: What if the freelancer raises their rates?
faq.a: It is normal over time. Discuss value and scope, and decide openly.

faq.q: How do I avoid depending on one person?
faq.a: Keep documentation, own your accounts and files, and know who could step in if needed.
